q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: WITH Bar1ServesCount AS (SELECT bar AS bar1, COUNT(beer) AS count1 FROM serves GROUP BY bar), Bar2ServesCount AS (SELECT bar AS bar2, COUNT(beer) AS count2 FROM serves GROUP BY bar), Bar1ServesBeer AS (SELECT bar1, count1, s.beer AS beer1 FROM Bar1ServesCount AS b1 INNER JOIN serves AS s ON b1.bar1 = s.bar), Bar2ServesBeer AS (SELECT bar2, count2, s.beer AS beer2 FROM Bar2ServesCount AS b2 INNER JOIN serves AS s ON b2.bar2 = s.bar), Bar1ProperSetBar2 AS (SELECT DISTINCT b2.bar2, b1.bar1 FROM Bar2ServesBeer AS b2 LEFT JOIN Bar1ServesBeer AS b1 ON b2.beer2 = b1.beer1 AND b2.bar2 <> b1.bar1 AND b2.count2 > b1.count1 WHERE NOT b1.bar1 IS NULL AND NOT b1.beer1 IS NULL) SELECT bar1, bar2 FROM Bar1ProperSetBar2

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks for bars that serve a beer which no other bar serves, and Q2 checks for bars that serve a beer which no other bar serves with a higher count.
counterexample_dsp: Q1 and Q2 will output different results when there are two bars, A and B, where A serves beer X and B serves beer Y, and both A and B serve beer Z with A serving more of Z than B.
